### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **8** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/plugin-email`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/service-messaging`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **65** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**35** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 171cf6d992d5144d235414df81d500c94abb8657`.

⛔ **16** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **189** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 171cf6d992d5144d235414df81d500c94abb8657` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `24fe813ceddd8512fc7841f961d400492c66a331` — the merge of head `1484ab596293460b5d7beb0dc355754e10f3ff4e` into base `171cf6d992d5144d235414df81d500c94abb8657`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 24fe813ceddd8512fc7841f961d400492c66a331 && git checkout 24fe813ceddd8512fc7841f961d400492c66a331
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 171cf6d992d5144d235414df81d500c94abb8657 1484ab596293460b5d7beb0dc355754e10f3ff4e && git checkout -B drift-repro 171cf6d992d5144d235414df81d500c94abb8657 && git merge --no-ff 1484ab596293460b5d7beb0dc355754e10f3ff4e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 171cf6d992d5144d235414df81d500c94abb8657
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 171cf6d992d5144d235414df81d500c94abb8657` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

**Epic red-line review of #32214 (#31699 PR 1/3, email_template) at head 4c176c5b: no PASS yet. One item is owed before landing.** I read the diff and body, but did not run them. Contract review and ACCEPT are seat 1's. Everything else holds against the three red lines.

**Owed: a legacy package-less row read under two holders. Ruling 6761802819 says it "must be refused for every covered type before that type narrows".** This PR narrows `email_template`, and the row is still served at both addresses.

- **Where.** In `exactQualifierItem`, a package-less row has no string `_packageId`, so the function returns it before any holder check. Both `?package=P1` and `?package=P2` then serve one environment row as each package's own.
- **Why this PR makes it reachable.** The widening lets a second namespace install a name P1 held alone. A package-less row written while P1 held the name was P1's customization (D4). Once P2 installs, P2's exact address serves P1's customization, which red line 1 forbids. This is reachable through install, not only through a clash sealed before Phase 1.
- **Do (small, and generic in `exactQualifierItem`, so it covers every type in `PACKAGE_SCOPED_READ_TYPES`):**
  1. When the read names a package, and the item has no package while two or more packages hold the name, refuse with `409 ambiguous-in-closure` naming every holder.
     - The `_env` address keeps serving the environment's own row.
     - With one holder, the row is that holder's customization, as today.
     - Apply the same rule to every read that layers the package-less row as a holder's overlay, including the send's registry loader for a package caller.
  2. `os migrate stored-references` lists such rows beside `pairMembers`, with their candidates, so the operator saves the row under one package.
  3. Pins: two holders refuse at both exact addresses; one holder serves; `_env` serves; an ablation.
- **Declare.** The narrowing covers `agent` and `skill`, which already narrowed on main with this gap, and the nine E8 types. Give FROM→TO and a first-party census.
- **Size.** If this pushes the PR past 3,000 lines, carry it as a precondition card that lands first. #32214 does not land with the path open.
- **Not owed here:** binding the row to the incumbent when a second holder arrives, as flows do after the seal. Refusing is fail-closed. A bind is a later card, if an operator asks for it.

**Holds:**
- **F1:**
  - The send resolves D3 from `callerPackageId`, and the `notify` node names the flow's armed package (`flowCallerPackage`), never the `_packageId` stamp.
  - A literal payload key with that name is dropped.
  - A send with no package keeps the environment item, then the one holder, then `409`.
  - With one holder, every name reads byte-identically to today.
- **F2:** a pair row with two possible owners is refused at both exact addresses and left out of both lists. A row that declares `overrides.package` is served only at that base.
- **Item 1:** `email_template` is slotted beside the namespace switch, with the superset pin and A9.
- **Item 4:** there is no redactor.
- **Item 5, accepted as #32183's class.** The doors count a disabled holder, so the failure is an over-refusal that names a disabled package. It is fail-closed, never a serve. It is declared, and #32183 fixes it once for every package-scoped type.
- **Red line 3:** three narrowings and the widening are declared, with first-party count 0. The platform-requested `auth.*` mails keep one holder per deployment.

The send carries the caller, the loader resolves by D3 from it, a two-holder name is read at the resolved holder's address, and a send with no package keeps environment item, then the one holder, then 409. Pinned at each rung. One spelling of the same reference is left on the old rule: F-A.

**`packages/spec/src/contracts/email-service.ts` (hits), against ADR-0150 D3 and its first consumers.** The member's contract is D3 as ruled: own, then the one holder in the declared closure, then a refusal naming every candidate; omitted or `null` keeps the bare-name meaning; the platform's auth mails resolve environment-wide. The first consumers agree with it: `EmailService` forwards it on every rung, the registry loader implements each step, and the two channels mirror it structurally with a compile-checked key. The one sentence that does not hold at its consumer is "A flow's `notify` node passes the package whose own flow body is armed" (F-A).

**F-A — must-fix. A packaged flow still resolves a template name environment-wide when the reference is written in the node's literal `payload`.**

- `notify-node.ts:1010` computes the caller only when `cfg.template` is set. `notify-node.ts:1178-1186` spreads the literal payload first and removes one key from it, `templateCallerPackageId` (`:740-744`). A literal `payload: { template: 'NAME' }` on a node with inline `title` / `message` survives into the emitted payload beside `title` and `body`.
- Both channels take the template path on that key alone (`email-channel.ts:485-488`, `inbox-channel.ts:178-181`) and ignore the inline strings. No caller was recorded, so `sendTemplate` / `renderTemplate` run with no package (`email-channel.ts:524-527`).
- The spec's `payload` is `z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())` and its refinement reads `cfg.template`, not `payload.template`, so nothing refuses the spelling at authoring.
- Result, read not run: from a package whose own body is armed, a template held only by a package outside its declared closure, or authored only in the environment, is served. That is the read narrowing (3) declares refused, and red line 1's "no environment-wide guess for a caller with a package". For a two-holder name the same spelling is refused on every send, the holder's own flow included, which is F1's failure for this spelling.
- The diff states the intent it does not meet: "an authored key can never resolve the template from another package" (`notify-node.ts:735-738`), and the contract file says the node passes the armed package.
- Not a regression (`main` resolves every send this way), and first-party use is 0 by the PR's own census of `template:` keys, which did not count this spelling. It is must-fix because ADR-0150 D9 narrows a type only after its doors carry the package, the epic ruling on F1 is that the `notify` node passes the armed package, and this is that node.
- Fix, either: record the caller whenever the emitted payload carries a template reference, whichever key wrote it; or drop `template` and `templateData` from the literal payload as the diff already drops `templateCallerPackageId`. Pin the literal spelling beside the existing "literal key dropped" case. If the epic seat instead rules the literal spelling outside the node's contract, the node must refuse or drop it, and the changeset says so.

**F-B — should-fix. A bound pair row is still served at the App's own address.**

- `protocol-exact-qualifier.ts:185` returns the item for the App's own pair before the declared base is read (`:191`), and `pairMemberWithheldAt` does the same at `:267` before `:269`.
- So when the App itself holds the name beside its member X, a row declaring `overrides.package: X` is served and listed at the App's address as well as X's.
- The function's own doc says such a row "is served on that base's address only", and the epic's pin is "after a bind, only the bound pair is served". The bind test holds the name in X and Y only, so the state is unpinned.
- Fix: read the declared base first in both functions, or pin the state with the answer the epic seat gives.

**F-C — should-fix. The report's remedy for an ambiguous pair row has no door.**

- The epic ruling asks that `os migrate stored-references` list the row "so the operator can bind it". The command prints "Declare in the row the package it customizes (overrides.package)" (`stored-references/index.ts:243`) and the module says the row is "Not bindable by `bind`" (`stored-package-references.ts:51`).
- Nothing in the diff writes that declaration, and `overrides` is ADR-0146 D2's declaration that an item replaces its base's same-named item whole (`override-declaration.zod.ts`). Here it is read as the binding of an added member, which replaces nothing. Whether the save door admits it on a member the base does not ship was not readable from the diff.
- Fix: name the door that writes it (or let `bind` write it), and pin that a row so written passes the save gate.

**F-D — should-fix. The legacy package-less row now reaches the send, and the changeset contradicts its own change.**

- With two holders, the list scoped to either holder seats the package-less row (`standInRows`), so each holder's send renders it. One holder's customization is sent as the other's. The declaration names only "both exact addresses serve it".
- `.changeset/...:34` says the row is "to be refused for every covered type before that type narrows", in the change that narrows `email_template` without refusing it.
- Fix: say in the changeset and the PR body that the sends of both holders render the row too, and replace the sentence with what is true here (this type narrows with the item open, under the epic seat's line asked for in ③). The report does not list such a row either; say so or list it.

**Implementing files, the rest.**

- `template-loader.ts`: agrees with the contract (① 3). Its doc sentence on a dependent's addition matches the code and the scoped list.
